items.problem: Bootstrap inventory omitted linked/shared UWP project items.
items.evidence: lessons.json missing_tooling[0]; session-log turn 2 copied 9 files while the csproj linked XAML, code, styles, and assets.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 only recursed below -Source and never evaluated explicit csproj Include/Link items.
items.change: Resolve common project path properties and explicit Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content/resource Include+Link items, copy them to logical Link paths, and include them in rewrite/triage/mapping.
items.expected_effect: Agents start from authored shared XAML and assets rather than obj output or manual reconstruction.
items.falsifiable_check: On this source the bootstrap reports 30 files with 21 linked items, and MainPage.xaml, all seven scenario XAML files, Styles/Styles.xaml, shared code, and linked assets exist in the target before any agent edit.

items.problem: Shell guidance encouraged redesign and omitted layout/scroll invariants.
items.evidence: skill-defects.json items 1-3; discrepancies.json reports changed shell/footer/theme, clipped headings, and clipped output in all seven scenarios.
items.root_cause: The prose incorrectly treated an SDK-sample ListView/Frame shell as a NavigationView migration even though its controls remain supported.
items.change: Correct shell mapping to preserve supported controls; restrict NavigationView adaptation; add visual invariants for resources/footer, wrapping, scroll boundaries, and available viewport.
items.expected_effect: Migrated shells retain source hierarchy and keep actions/output reachable within the initial window.
items.falsifiable_check: On rerun the candidate uses the source SplitView/ListBox/Frame shell with footer/resources; no heading crosses the right edge and every scenario output is reachable inside its preserved ScrollViewer.
items.tier_justification: A template cannot safely choose visual structure for arbitrary source shells; after Tier 1 supplies the real XAML, semantic preservation remains judgement work. The prose must remove the actively wrong substitution.

items.problem: The skill prescribed nonexistent winapp build commands.
items.root_cause: Compilation and winapp launch responsibilities were conflated.
items.change: Replace winapp build with dotnet build <path-to-csproj> and explicitly state that winapp has no build subcommand.
items.expected_effect: Build steps terminate successfully using the supported compiler path.
items.falsifiable_check: A rerun contains no 'build was not matched' CLI error and the final dotnet build exits 0.
items.tier_justification: The validator already implements Tier 1 build enforcement correctly; the defect is the contradictory user-facing command text.
